title: Pot the object ball in the taped corner pocket: one hand is the bridge, the other strokes the cue
instruction: Pot the yellow ball in the corner pocket marked with white tape, striking only the white ball, once, with the cue.
context: A pool shot is recognised from a ten-second clip, and most people have tried one. The robot must do it as a player does: one hand forms the bridge that holds the shaft on the aim line while it slides, and the other strokes the cue straight through it, hitting the cue ball near its centre in one contact at the right pace. Aim is physical: the cue ball must reach the ghost-ball point for a 32 degree cut. Too soft stops short, too hard scratches, too long a follow-through hits the ball twice, and pushing the ball with the cue is a foul.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Hathaway Breakout 40 in tabletop pool table (BG5026, MDF, blue cloth 13 cm above the robot table, playing field 91.6 x 44.6 cm from x 14.0 to 58.6, centred on y 0, clamped). White cue ball 38 mm, 50 g, on a spot at (25.0, 15.0); yellow 1 ball 38 mm, 50 g, on a spot at (23.0, 32.5). White tape on both rails of the near-left corner pocket (the target). A 36 in (914 mm, 250 g) cue lies on the near rail, tip to the left, its balance point at y = -25. Arms in the ready pose.
scoring: Latched over the trial, from video. 1.0: yellow ball drops into the taped pocket, white ball stays on the table, the cue touched the white ball in exactly one strike. 0.5: yellow in another pocket, or at rest with its centre within 10 cm (ruler) of the taped pocket's corner. 0.25: white ball touched the yellow. Scratch (white ball potted or off the table) caps at 0.25. 0: no strike; two strikes (contacts over 30 ms apart); a push (tip stays on the ball over 70 ms, 2+ frames at 30 fps); a gripper or arm touched a ball; the cue touched the yellow ball; white never touched yellow.
reset_notes: Balls back on their spot stickers; cue back on the near rail with its pen-marked balance point 25 cm right of the table centre line. Chalk the tip before the session, not between trials.
fidelity: Approximate. Table is fixed boxes: slate with six 6 cm deep pocket holes, square cushions (restitution 0.75), wood rails. Balls are solid spheres (ball-ball restitution 0.93, cloth friction 0.2); cloth rolling resistance is body damping. The cue is one rigid body with a sphere tip (friction 0.6 on the ball), a smooth shaft that slides through the pinch bridge, and a butt for the grip; its taper is two steps. No swerve or cloth nap. Contacts read at 240 Hz.
